title: Route Handlers
description: Learn how Next.js Route Handlers let you build APIs directly inside the App Router using familiar file conventions and Web Request/Response objects.

data.text: Route Handlers are how Next.js App Router applications expose API endpoints. Instead of creating separate API route files, you define endpoints directly inside `app/` using a `route.ts` file. This keeps your API code close to the UI that uses it.

A Route Handler is a TypeScript file named `route.ts` (or `route.js`) inside any `app/` folder. It exports functions named after HTTP methods: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, or `DELETE`. Next.js turns each exported function into an endpoint at that folder's URL path.

items: Use `route.ts` inside any segment folder, not just `app/api/`
Each exported function name must match an HTTP method in uppercase
The function receives a standard `Request` object and returns a `Response`
Dynamic routes work with `[param]` folders just like page routes

data.text: Imagine you want an endpoint that returns a list of published posts. Create `app/posts/route.ts` and export a `GET` function that reads from your data source.

data.title: GET route handler returning JSON

data.text: Notice that `NextResponse.json()` is a small helper that sets the `Content-Type: application/json` header for you. You can also use the native Web API `Response.json()` or build a `Response` manually.

Reading the request body is straightforward. Route Handlers give you a standard `Request` object, so you call `request.json()`, `request.text()`, `request.formData()`, or `request.blob()` depending on what the client sends.

data.title: POST route handler creating a resource
Validate Before You Trust
data.text: Anything a browser sends can be forged or malformed. Always validate `request.json()` with a schema library like Zod before using the data. Never assume the shape of the body is correct.

If your endpoint needs to act on a specific resource, add a dynamic segment folder. For example, `app/posts/[id]/route.ts` matches `/posts/123`. The `params` object gives you access to the segment value.

data.title: Dynamic route handler with params
Key Takeaways
items: Route Handlers live in `app/` as `route.ts` files, keeping APIs alongside UI
Export functions named after HTTP methods: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`
Use standard Web `Request` and `Response` APIs, or `NextResponse` helpers
Dynamic segments use `[param]` folders with typed `params`
